tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Despite the heavy rain, we finished the outdoor photography session.
Despite of the heavy rain, we finished the outdoor photography session.
Although the heavy rain, we finished the outdoor photography session.
Because the delay, the museum tour started twenty minutes late.
The picnic was cancelled owing a sudden thunderstorm.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "Despite" takes a noun phrase directly, so "Despite the heavy rain" is well formed before the main clause.

Tip: If you can replace the linker with "in spite of," you almost always want a noun, not a full clause.

FALSE — Never write "despite of." Use "despite the heavy rain" or "in spite of the heavy rain."

Tip: "Despite of" is one of the most common exam traps — delete "of" on sight.

FALSE — "Although" needs a clause with a verb: "Although it rained heavily," not a bare noun phrase.

Tip: Ask "is there a finite verb after although?" If not, switch to despite / in spite of.

FALSE — "Because" introduces a clause; for a noun use "because of the delay" (or "Because there was a delay").

Tip: "Because" + noun is almost always wrong — insert "of" or rebuild as a full clause.

FALSE — The fixed pattern is "owing to" + noun: "owing to a sudden thunderstorm."

Tip: Treat "owing to" as one unit; if "to" is missing, the sentence fails.
tasks.solution_overview: This set checks whether you pick the right linker shape: noun after despite / because of / owing to, and a full clause after although / because. Read each connector and ask what kind of material follows it before you mark true or false.

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: In spite of the crowded platform, Maya found a seat on the morning train.
Although the crowded platform, Maya found a seat on the morning train.
The trail was icy; however, the hikers still reached the summit café.
The trail was icy, however the hikers still reached the summit café without stronger punctuation.
The concert started late owing technical problems with the sound desk.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "In spite of" + noun phrase is the correct concessive pattern here.

Tip: "In spite of" and "despite" are interchangeable before a noun; neither takes a bare clause.

FALSE — "Although" needs a clause with a verb: "Although the platform was crowded…"

Tip: A noun after although is almost always a despite transplant — rewrite or switch linker.

TRUE — As a conjunctive adverb, "however" sits well after a semicolon (or full stop) between two independent clauses.

Tip: Semicolon / period + however + comma is the clean formal pattern.

FALSE — A bare comma before conjunctive "however" is weak or wrong in formal writing; prefer a semicolon or a new sentence.

Tip: If however could start a new sentence, do not glue it with only a comma.

FALSE — Restore the full linker: "owing to technical problems."

Tip: "Owing" without "to" is never complete in this pattern.
tasks.solution_overview: Contrast linkers come in two families: despite / in spite of (noun) versus although (clause), plus however between full sentences. Check punctuation around however and whether owing to is complete.

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Because of the closed bridge, cyclists took the riverside path instead.
Because the bridge was closed, cyclists took the riverside path instead.
Even though the recipe looked complicated, Leo baked the cake successfully.
Even though the complicated recipe, Leo baked the cake successfully.
Whereas the first half was quiet, the second half of the match was frantic.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "Because of" + noun phrase correctly gives the reason.

Tip: Use because of before nouns; reserve bare because for clauses.

TRUE — "Because" + full clause is the other correct reason pattern.

Tip: If you already have subject + verb after because, do not add "of."

TRUE — "Even though" takes a clause, and "the recipe looked complicated" supplies one.

Tip: Even though ≈ although: both want finite clauses.

FALSE — "Even though" cannot take a noun phrase alone; write "even though the recipe looked complicated."

Tip: Swap even though → despite when only a noun follows.

TRUE — "Whereas" contrasts two full clauses cleanly.

Tip: Whereas needs clause + clause; "whereas a quiet first half" without a verb is wrong.
tasks.solution_overview: Cause and concession each have a clause form and a noun form. Match because / even though / whereas to clauses, and because of to nouns — that single check resolves most of these items.

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Despite of repeated reminders, Nina forgot to water the balcony plants.
In spite the repeated reminders, Nina forgot to water the balcony plants.
Although Nina forgot to water the plants, they somehow survived the weekend.
The library was quiet because of a school holiday in the neighbourhood.
Tickets sold out early; however, a few returns appeared at the box office.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — Drop "of": "Despite repeated reminders…"

Tip: Despite never partners with of; in spite always needs of.

FALSE — The full phrase is "in spite of," not "in spite" alone.

Tip: Remember the trio: despite / in spite of / although — learn the prepositions as fixed spelling.

TRUE — Although + clause correctly sets up the contrast with the main clause.

Tip: When the concessive idea has its own verb, although is usually safer than despite.

TRUE — Because of + noun phrase is the right causal linker here.

Tip: A school holiday is a noun phrase, so because of (not bare because) is required.

TRUE — Semicolon + however correctly joins two contrasting independent clauses.

Tip: Read however as a sentence adverb: it likes strong punctuation before it.
tasks.solution_overview: Watch the spelling pairs: despite (no of) versus in spite of (of required). Then confirm although and however are doing clause-level work with proper punctuation.

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Owing to thick fog, the ferry crossing was postponed until noon.
Because of thick fog, the ferry crossing was postponed until noon.
Despite the fog lingering all morning, several walkers still set out.
Although the fog lingered all morning, several walkers still set out.
However, the coastal path remained closed for safety checks.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "Owing to" + noun phrase correctly states the cause.

Tip: Formal notices often prefer owing to / because of before abstract nouns like fog.

TRUE — "Because of" + noun phrase is an equally correct causal pattern here.

Tip: Because of and owing to are near-interchangeable before nouns.

TRUE — Despite can take a gerund noun phrase ("the fog lingering all morning").

Tip: Despite + -ing phrase is fine; despite + finite clause usually is not.

TRUE — Although + finite clause ("lingered") is the clean concessive form.

Tip: If you can hear a tensed verb after although, the clause test usually passes.

TRUE — Sentence-initial "However," with a following comma correctly opens a contrast.

Tip: Starting with However is fine; just do not leave it mid-sentence with only a weak comma before it.
tasks.solution_overview: Here the traps sit in small words: the missing to after owing, and the wrong follow-on after although versus despite. Read the material after each linker as carefully as the linker itself.

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The rehearsal stopped because of a broken stage light.
The rehearsal stopped because a stage light was broken.
The rehearsal stopped because of a stage light was broken.
In spite of the broken light, the cast finished Act Two.
Whereas the lighting failed, the orchestra kept perfect timing.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Because of + noun phrase correctly explains the stoppage.

Tip: A broken stage light is a noun — because of fits.

TRUE — Because + clause is equally correct when you spell out subject + verb.

Tip: Both because and because of can be right; the grammar after them decides.

FALSE — Do not stack "because of" onto a full clause; drop "of" or rewrite the clause as a noun.

Tip: "Because of + subject + verb" is almost always a false hybrid.

TRUE — In spite of + noun phrase is the right concessive frame.

Tip: The broken light is a noun idea — in spite of / despite both work.

TRUE — Whereas contrasts two complete clauses about lighting versus the orchestra.

Tip: Use whereas for side-by-side contrasts, not for simple cause.
highlights: because of a stage light was
tasks.solution_overview: Cause linkers are easy until someone glues because of onto a whole clause. Check that after because of you only have a noun idea, and after because / whereas you have a real clause.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Despite the fact that the kitchen was tiny, they hosted a lively dinner.
Despite that the kitchen was tiny, they hosted a lively dinner.
Although the kitchen was tiny, they hosted a lively dinner.
The kitchen was tiny. However, the dinner still felt generous.
Space was limited however the hosts somehow seated twelve guests comfortably.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — "Despite the fact that" + clause is an accepted formal workaround when you need a clause after despite.

Tip: Prefer plain although when you can; despite the fact that is wordy but grammatical.

FALSE — "Despite that" + clause is non-standard in careful exam English; use although or despite the fact that.

Tip: If you want a clause, switch to although rather than forcing despite.

TRUE — Although + clause is the cleanest concessive choice here.

Tip: When both options work, although is usually shorter and safer than despite the fact that.

TRUE — A full stop before However correctly separates the contrasting sentences.

Tip: Period + However + comma is as strong as semicolon + however.

FALSE — Running however between clauses with no strong punctuation is incorrect in formal writing.

Tip: Never leave however floating between clauses with zero commas or stops.
tasks.solution_overview: Despite wants nouns; although wants clauses; however wants sentence-level punctuation. These five lines test those three habits in a dinner-party story.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Owing to a power cut, the cinema switched to an earlier screening.
Because of a power cut, the cinema switched to an earlier screening.
Although the power cut, the cinema switched to an earlier screening.
In spite of the power cut, the audience stayed in their seats.
Whereas the power cut, the audience stayed in their seats.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Owing to + noun correctly marks the cause of the schedule change.

Tip: Owing to and because of are near twins before nouns.

TRUE — Because of + noun is equally correct in the same slot.

Tip: Either linker works; do not mix them with although’s clause rule.

FALSE — Although needs "Although there was a power cut" or similar, not a bare noun.

Tip: Power cut is a noun — feed it to despite / because of / owing to instead.

TRUE — In spite of + noun correctly frames the concession.

Tip: Staying seated despite a power cut is a classic despite / in spite of pattern.

FALSE — Whereas requires a full clause, not a noun phrase.

Tip: Rewrite as "Whereas the power failed…" or switch to despite.
tasks.solution_overview: Same noun idea — the power cut — can follow owing to, because of, or in spite of, but not although or whereas. Let the linker dictate the grammar of what follows.

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The experiment succeeded despite early doubts from the lab team.
The experiment succeeded in spite of early doubts from the lab team.
The experiment succeeded although early doubts from the lab team.
Early doubts were widespread; however, the results still matched the prediction.
Early doubts were widespread, the results however still matched the prediction with no change in word order.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Despite + noun phrase correctly expresses concession after the main clause.

Tip: Mid- or end-sentence despite is fine when a noun follows.

TRUE — In spite of mirrors despite before the same noun phrase.

Tip: Prefer one style consistently in a report; both are grammatical.

FALSE — Although cannot take "early doubts…" without a verb.

Tip: "Although the team had doubts" would repair it.

TRUE — Semicolon + however correctly contrasts doubts with the successful results.

Tip: Keep a comma after however in this pattern.

FALSE — Dropping however into the middle without proper clause punctuation makes the sentence clumsy and formally wrong here.

Tip: Put however at the clause edge with a semicolon or period, not as a loose insert.
tasks.solution_overview: Concession after a success statement usually wants despite / in spite of + noun. Although needs a clause, and however needs clear sentence boundaries — do not bury it mid-clause.

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Because of rising pollen levels, many runners skipped the morning jog.
Because pollen levels were rising, many runners skipped the morning jog.
Because of pollen levels were rising, many runners skipped the morning jog.
Even though pollen levels were high, a few athletes still trained outdoors.
Even though high pollen levels, a few athletes still trained outdoors.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Because of + noun phrase correctly states the reason.

Tip: Rising pollen levels behaves as a noun idea after because of.

TRUE — Because + finite clause is the matching clause form.

Tip: Keep because of and because as a clean pair: noun versus clause.

FALSE — Because of must not introduce a full clause with were.

Tip: If you see a tensed verb after because of, rewrite immediately.

TRUE — Even though + clause correctly marks concession.

Tip: Even though and although share the same clause requirement.

FALSE — Even though cannot take a bare noun phrase.

Tip: Switch to despite high pollen levels, or add a verb after even though.
tasks.solution_overview: Cause and concession swap partners easily: because of / despite take nouns; because / even though take clauses. Spot the hybrid "because of + were" and the bare noun after even though.

tasks.title: Task 11
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: She kept painting, although her wrist ached after every session.
She kept painting despite her wrist ached after every session.
She kept painting in spite of her aching wrist.
Her wrist ached; she continued, however, with shorter sessions.
Her wrist ached, however she continued with shorter sessions using only a comma.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Although + finite clause correctly softens the contrast.

Tip: Pain + continued activity is a natural although pattern.

FALSE — Despite cannot take the finite clause "her wrist ached."

Tip: Use although, or "despite her aching wrist."

TRUE — In spite of + noun phrase is the correct concessive noun form.

Tip: Convert the clause idea into a noun (aching wrist) for in spite of / despite.

TRUE — Parenthetical however between commas correctly contrasts ache with persistence.

Tip: Mid-clause however with commas on both sides is allowed.

FALSE — However joining two clauses with only a preceding comma is a classic splice error.

Tip: Semicolon or period before however when it links full clauses.
tasks.solution_overview: This set contrasts clause linkers with noun linkers around the same idea, then checks two however patterns: legal parenthetical commas versus an illegal comma splice.

tasks.title: Task 12
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Owing to roadworks on the ring road, the coach arrived forty minutes late.
Owing roadworks on the ring road, the coach arrived forty minutes late.
Despite roadworks slowing traffic, several passengers still made their connections.
Although roadworks slowing traffic, several passengers still made their connections.
Whereas the outbound coach was late, the return journey ran on time.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Owing to + noun correctly explains the late arrival.

Tip: Travel notices often open with owing to + cause.

FALSE — Missing to: write "owing to roadworks."

Tip: Scan for orphan "owing" without "to."

TRUE — Despite + -ing phrase ("roadworks slowing traffic") is grammatical.

Tip: Despite + noun/-ing ≈ although + clause.

FALSE — Although needs a finite verb: "Although roadworks slowed traffic…"

Tip: "Although + -ing" without a clear subject is a frequent transfer error.

TRUE — Whereas contrasts two complete clauses about outbound versus return.

Tip: Whereas likes balanced clause pairs, not noun fragments.
tasks.solution_overview: Check owing to completeness, then decide whether an -ing phrase belongs after despite (yes) or after although (usually no). Whereas still demands two full clauses.

tasks.title: Task 13
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The choir performed well despite having had only two rehearsals that week.
The choir performed well although having had only two rehearsals that week.
Because of having only two rehearsals, the conductor shortened the programme.
Because having only two rehearsals, the conductor shortened the programme.
Having had only two rehearsals; however, the choir still sounded confident.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Despite + perfect gerund phrase correctly marks concession.

Tip: Despite + having (had) … is a polished formal pattern.

FALSE — Although needs a finite clause: "Although the choir had had only two rehearsals…"

Tip: Do not transplant a despite -ing phrase under although.

TRUE — Because of + gerund noun phrase correctly states the cause.

Tip: Because of can take -ing phrases that act like nouns.

FALSE — Bare because needs subject + verb, not a hanging -ing phrase.

Tip: Add of, or rewrite: "Because they had only two rehearsals…"

FALSE — A dangling -ing opener cannot be glued to however with only a semicolon in this broken shape; rebuild as two full clauses.

Tip: However still needs a proper independent clause before and after it.
tasks.solution_overview: Advanced concession and cause often use -ing phrases. They fit after despite / because of, but not after bare although / because, and they cannot rescue a malformed however pair.

tasks.title: Task 14
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: In spite of what the guidebook claimed, the gallery was still closed on Mondays.
Despite what the guidebook claimed, the gallery was still closed on Mondays.
Although what the guidebook claimed, the gallery was still closed on Mondays.
The guidebook was outdated; the gallery, however, posted clear opening hours online.
The guidebook was outdated however the gallery posted clear opening hours online.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — In spite of + free relative ("what…") works because the what-clause acts as a noun.

Tip: What/how clauses can follow in spite of / despite / because of.

TRUE — Despite + the same what-clause is equally correct.

Tip: Despite and in spite of share this noun-like object pattern.

FALSE — Although needs an ordinary clause, not "although what…" without a verb frame.

Tip: Prefer "Although the guidebook claimed otherwise…"

TRUE — Parenthetical however between commas correctly contrasts outdated print with online hours.

Tip: Commas both sides signal parenthetical however, not a splice.

FALSE — No strong punctuation before however between two clauses.

Tip: Insert a semicolon or start a new sentence.
tasks.solution_overview: Wh-clauses behave like nouns after despite / in spite of, but although still wants a normal subject–verb clause. Pair that with a careful however punctuation check.

tasks.title: Task 15
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Whereas most guests preferred the terrace, a few stayed indoors near the fireplace.
Despite most guests preferred the terrace, a few stayed indoors near the fireplace.
In spite of most guests preferring the terrace, a few stayed indoors near the fireplace.
Because of most guests preferring the terrace, the hosts moved the buffet outside.
Although most guests preferring the terrace, the hosts moved the buffet outside.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Whereas + finite clause correctly opens a balanced contrast.

Tip: Whereas needs a tensed verb in each half of the contrast.

FALSE — Despite cannot take "most guests preferred…" as a finite clause.

Tip: Switch to although, or to "despite most guests preferring…"

TRUE — In spite of + -ing phrase correctly compresses the same idea.

Tip: Preferring turns the clause into a noun-like object for in spite of.

TRUE — Because of + -ing phrase correctly marks cause.

Tip: The same -ing phrase can serve cause (because of) or concession (in spite of).

FALSE — Although still needs "Although most guests preferred…" with a finite verb.

Tip: Final check on every although: find the tensed verb or mark false.
highlights: In spite of most guests preferring
tasks.solution_overview: One party detail — terrace versus indoors — is reshaped under five linkers. Name the linker, name what follows it, and the true/false call becomes mechanical.

tasks.title: Task 16
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: In spite of having little free time, Sam joined the weekend cycling club.
Despite of having little free time, Sam joined the weekend cycling club.
Although having little free time, Sam joined the weekend cycling club.
Although he had little free time, Sam joined the weekend cycling club.
Free time was scarce; however, the club rides still felt restorative.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — In spite of + having… correctly frames concession with a gerund.

Tip: Having + noun after in spite of / despite is a reliable pattern.

FALSE — Remove of: "Despite having little free time…"

Tip: Despite + -ing is fine; despite of + -ing is not.

FALSE — Although does not take a bare -ing phrase in careful formal English; add a subject + finite verb.

Tip: "Although having…" is a common L2 transfer error from despite.

TRUE — Although + full clause repairs the previous pattern.

Tip: Insert a clear subject (he / Sam) after although when in doubt.

TRUE — Semicolon + however correctly contrasts scarce time with the value of the rides.

Tip: Keep however’s comma after the linker.
tasks.solution_overview: Gerund concessions after in spite of / despite are elegant, but although still wants a full clause. Watch the fake "despite of" and the fake "although -ing" twins.

tasks.title: Task 17
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: The match resumed, owing to a brief break in the storm clouds.
The match resumed owing a brief break in the storm clouds.
A break in the clouds arrived; the pitch, however, remained too wet for play.
A break in the clouds arrived, however the pitch remained too wet for play with only a comma before however.
Despite a break in the clouds arriving, several seats in the stand stayed empty.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Mid-sentence "owing to" + noun phrase correctly states the cause.

Tip: A comma before owing to is common when the cause follows the result.

FALSE — Missing to: write "owing to a brief break."

Tip: End-of-sentence owing still needs its to.

TRUE — Parenthetical however between commas correctly contrasts the break with the wet pitch.

Tip: Mid-clause however with commas is allowed when it does not join two bare clauses with a weak comma alone.

FALSE — Using however as a coordinator with only a preceding comma remains poor formal style.

Tip: Distinguish parenthetical however (commas both sides) from clause-joining however (semicolon/period).

TRUE — Despite + -ing phrase correctly marks concession.

Tip: "Despite X arriving" ≈ "although X arrived."
highlights: Despite a break in the clouds arriving
tasks.solution_overview: Harder however items distinguish parenthetical mid-clause use from illegal comma splices. Pair that with a clean owing to check and a despite -ing concession.

tasks.title: Task 18
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Because of how abruptly the trail narrowed, the group slowed to single file.
Because how abruptly the trail narrowed, the group slowed to single file.
Although how abruptly the trail narrowed surprised the guides, nobody turned back.
In spite of how abruptly the trail narrowed, nobody turned back.
The trail narrowed abruptly. Owing to that change, the group slowed to single file.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Because of + free relative noun clause ("how abruptly…") is grammatical.

Tip: Wh-clauses can act as nouns after because of / despite / in spite of.

FALSE — Bare because needs a normal clause, not "because how…" without of.

Tip: If a how/what clause follows, you usually need because of, not bare because.

TRUE — Although + clause including "how abruptly…surprised" is fine.

Tip: Here the how-clause sits inside a larger finite clause — although is satisfied.

TRUE — In spite of + how-clause (noun-like) correctly marks concession.

Tip: In spite of how / despite what are polished formal patterns.

TRUE — Sentence-initial Owing to + noun correctly links to the prior change.

Tip: Pointing back with "that change" keeps owing to attached to a noun.
tasks.solution_overview: Advanced items use how-clauses as noun objects of because of / in spite of. Bare because still wants an ordinary subject–verb clause — do not drop of before how.

tasks.title: Task 19
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Notwithstanding the delayed train, the friends still made the exhibition opening — and despite the same delay, they refused to skip the café stop.
Despite delayed trains, they reached the gallery; however, several rooms had already closed for cleaning.
Although delayed trains, they reached the gallery, however several rooms had already closed for cleaning.
Owing to the delayed train, they walked the last kilometre along the canal.
Because of delayed trains were overcrowded, they walked the last kilometre along the canal.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Despite + noun works in the second half; the sentence remains grammatical (notwithstanding sits outside the core trap set but does not break the despite use).

Tip: Focus on the despite + noun chunk — it is correctly formed.

TRUE — Despite + noun and semicolon + however are both well formed.

Tip: Stacking two contrast tools is fine if each obeys its own rule.

FALSE — Although lacks a clause, and however is joined with only a weak comma.

Tip: Two linker errors can hide in one sentence — check each separately.

TRUE — Owing to + noun correctly states the reason for walking.

Tip: Travel delays often pair with owing to in formal notices.

FALSE — Because of + finite clause is illegal; write "Because trains were delayed" or "Because of overcrowded delayed trains."

Tip: If a verb like were sits after because of, rewrite immediately.
tasks.solution_overview: Dense sentences may contain two linkers. Score each linker on its own rule — noun versus clause, and however’s punctuation — rather than judging the sentence by overall "feel."

tasks.title: Task 20
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Whereas membership rose at the community garden, weekend volunteering fell — a split that, however, the organisers refused to call a failure.
Despite membership rose at the community garden, weekend volunteering fell.
In spite of membership rising at the community garden, weekend volunteering fell.
Because of membership rising at the community garden, the organisers ordered more tools.
Although membership rising at the community garden, the organisers ordered more tools.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Whereas opens a proper clause contrast, and parenthetical however is correctly set off with commas.

Tip: Parenthetical however does not replace a missing verb after whereas.

FALSE — Despite cannot take the finite clause "membership rose…"

Tip: Change to although, or to "despite the rise in membership."

TRUE — In spite of + -ing phrase correctly compresses the contrast.

Tip: Rising turns the clause idea into a noun-like phrase for in spite of.

TRUE — Because of + -ing phrase correctly marks cause.

Tip: Same -ing phrase can follow because of (cause) or in spite of (contrast).

FALSE — Although still needs "Although membership rose…" with a finite verb.

Tip: Final check on every although: find the tensed verb or mark false.
tasks.solution_overview: The last set mixes whereas, despite, in spite of, because of, and although around one community-garden story. Name the linker, name what follows it, and the true/false call becomes mechanical even at exam speed.
